summary: 48 top-level test functions across access_test.go/middleware_test.go/metrics_test.go cover all 16 TDD-Anchor cases plus substantial bonus coverage (extra edge cases, state-unchanged assertions on nearly every negative branch). All six flagged design decisions are architecturally sound and faithful to the spec — including catching a real discrepancy between tasks/5.md's TDD Anchor prose and Decision 18's actual rule, which the implementer resolved correctly in favor of Decision 18. However, three concrete coverage gaps let real regressions slip through: (1) the leak-test's admin-route subtests never reach AccessHandler's own error-wrapping code because RequireAdmin's authorization gate call fails first on the same unconditional stub error, leaving ListUsers's (and effectively SetAccess's) repository-error handling completely untested; (2) the three UnknownField/MissingGrantedField/EmptyBody 400 tests assert status code only, so a regression to the leaky err.Error() pattern used elsewhere in http.go would pass unnoticed, defeating the very design decision (#6) these tests exist to lock down; (3) no test anywhere verifies that cmd/main.go's future newMux actually threads cfg.CookieSecure/cfg.AllowedOrigins into BuildRoutes — the class of bug this whole task exists to close. None of these are exotic: each is a specific, fixable stub/test-design change, not a fundamental restructuring.

findings.issue: The leak test sets only `fixture.users.getErr` for all 5 subtests. For the 'GET /api/v1/admin/users' and 'POST /api/v1/admin/users/{login}/access' subtests, the request is gated by RequireAdmin, which itself calls resolveAccessState -> access.GetAccessState -> userRepo.GetUser("RoGogDBD") to check the caller's role. Because getErr fires unconditionally regardless of which login is looked up, RequireAdmin's own gate check fails and returns 500 *before the request ever reaches AccessHandler*. The test still passes (500, no leak), but it never exercises the handler's own error-wrapping of a ListUsers (or SetAccess) repository failure — it only re-proves that RequireAdmin's gate doesn't leak, which middleware_test.go already covers independently. The stub's `listErr` field exists specifically for isolating this scenario but is never set by any test in the suite. Litmus test: comment out AccessHandler's error handling on ListUsers entirely (e.g. write err.Error() straight to the body) -- this test suite would not catch it, because 3 of the 5 leak-test subtests (admin GET, admin POST, and 'GET /api/v1/users/{login}/chats' which is blocked the same way by RequireAccess) never reach handler-owned code.
findings.recommendation: Give stubUserRepo per-login error injection instead of one global error (e.g. `getErrByLogin map[string]error`, checked in GetUser by argument), or split into two knobs: one that only fires for the specific target login used by ListUsers/SetAccess and not for the admin's own identity lookup. Then add a case to TestWriteAPIDomainError_NoInternalTextLeak (or a new dedicated test) where the calling admin's own GetUser succeeds (gate passes) but `listErr` is set -- asserting 500/internal_error/no-leak from AccessHandler.ListUsers itself. Do the equivalent for SetAccess: gate passes for the admin, but the internal GetUser/SetAccess call on the target login fails.

findings.issue: All three tests assert only `recorder.Code != http.StatusBadRequest`; none inspect the response body. Design decision #6 (evaluated separately, and sound: a fixed 'invalid_request'-style slug plus server-side log, not writeAPIError(w,400,err.Error())) has no test locking it in. If the implementation instead used the pattern already present elsewhere in http.go for decodeJSON errors -- writeAPIError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error()) -- these three tests would still pass, silently leaking decodeJSON's raw text (e.g. `invalid json: json: unknown field "role"`) into the response. That is precisely the leak class Decision 17 closes off; a regression here is exactly as serious as the SQL-leak scenario TestWriteAPIDomainError_NoInternalTextLeak checks for, but on a code path that test doesn't touch (decodeJSON errors never reach writeAPIDomainError/classifyDomainError -- they are a distinct 400 source).
findings.recommendation: Add `if got := errorCode(t, recorder); got != "invalid_request" { t.Errorf(...) }` (or whatever fixed slug the implementation settles on) to all three tests, plus an explicit assertion that the raw decode error text is absent, e.g. `if strings.Contains(recorder.Body.String(), "unknown field") { t.Errorf("leaked decodeJSON text: %q", recorder.Body.String()) }`.

findings.location: server/cmd/main.go:63,87 (current newMux, pre-Task-5) and server/cmd/main_test.go:16-28 (testMux helper, pre-Task-5) -- design decision #1
findings.issue: Design decision #1 plans BuildRoutes(RouteDeps{...}) in package handler with main.go's newMux becoming a thin delegate. There is no import-cycle risk (handler does not import main; main already imports handler) -- that part of the decision is sound. But nothing written so far verifies that the *real* cfg-derived values actually flow into RouteDeps: access_test.go and middleware_test.go construct RouteDeps by hand from a fixture-local `*config.Config{...}` and a fixture-controlled cookieSecure/allowedOrigins pair, never touching config.Load() or the future newMux. The specific values Task 4 flagged as easy to get wrong -- `RouteDeps.CookieSecure` must come from `cfg.CookieSecure`, not be hardcoded or left at Go's zero-value `false`; `RouteDeps.AllowedOrigins` must come from `splitCSV(cfg.AllowedOrigins)` -- have zero test coverage of the main.go wiring itself. This is exactly the bug class the task exists to close (Task 4: middleware written, never connected); a newMux that forgets to pass cfg.CookieSecure through would compile, and every currently-written test (which all bypass newMux entirely) would still pass. cmd/main_test.go is not part of this round's changed files, so there is no draft to review against the decision's own claim that it 'genuinely still exercises production wiring' -- that claim is currently unverifiable, and the existing (pre-Task-5) file's testMux still calls the old two-arg newMux signature, so it will not even compile once newMux's signature changes.
findings.recommendation: As part of implementation (not just this test-design round), extend cmd/main_test.go's testMux to build cfg with non-default CookieSecure/AllowedOrigins and call the new newMux, then assert -- via a request through the real mux, following the existing TestNewMux_SameOriginGuardRejectsForeignOriginOnLogin pattern -- that RequireSameOrigin on the newly-wired prefixes actually reflects those cfg values (e.g. an Origin matching r.Host under secure=true with a https scheme passes, the same Origin under secure=false does not). Treat this as a blocking follow-up before code-round review, not an optional nicety, since it is the only place a cfg-to-RouteDeps wiring mistake could be caught.

findings.location: server/internal/service/access_test.go (no ListUsers test exists); server/internal/service/access.go (ListUsers not yet added, per design decision #3)
findings.issue: Task 2 established the convention that every AccessService method gets a dedicated stub-based unit test in service/access_test.go (EnsureUser, GetAccessState, CreateRequest, SetAccess all have one). The new AccessService.ListUsers -- decision #3, itself sound and non-interface-breaking -- has no planned unit test; it is only exercised indirectly through the full HTTP stack via access_test.go's TestAdminUsers_AsAdmin200 (happy path only). Combined with finding #1 above (the HTTP-level error path never reaches ListUsers either), the method's error-propagation behavior (does it wrap with %w like every sibling method, does it stay a pure passthrough as decision #3 promises) has no test anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Add a small TestAccessService_ListUsers in service/access_test.go using the existing userRepoStub: one case asserting the repository's records pass through unmodified, one case asserting a repository error is returned via errors.Is/errors.Unwrap (not swallowed or replaced).

findings.issue: Acceptance Criteria explicitly names 'CONTACT_EMAIL читается из окружения и попадает в ответ GET /api/v1/access/me' as one behavior to verify. TestAccessMe_ContactEmailComesFromConfig only proves the second half: given a value already sitting in a hand-built *config.Config{...}, AccessHandler serves it correctly. It never calls config.Load(), so nothing confirms Load() actually reads the CONTACT_EMAIL env var via envOrDefault. No config_test.go exists in the repo at all today, so this is a pre-existing house-style gap (none of the ~15 other env-backed fields are tested either), which makes this a minor rather than major finding -- but since this task is the one explicitly adding and naming the field, closing it here is cheap.
findings.recommendation: Add a minimal test in a new config_test.go: `t.Setenv("CONTACT_EMAIL", "x@example.com"); cfg, _ := config.Load(); if cfg.ContactEmail != "x@example.com" { ... }`, plus a default-empty-string case with the env var unset.

designDecisionNotes.1_BuildRoutes_placement: Sound: handler package does not import main, main already imports handler, so BuildRoutes living in package handler with main.go's newMux delegating to it creates no import cycle. Unverifiable claim: whether cmd/main_test.go 'genuinely still exercises production wiring' cannot be confirmed yet because that file is untouched this round and will not compile against a changed newMux signature -- see major finding above.
designDecisionNotes.2_MemoryRepository_no_admin_role: Confirmed genuine and unavoidable by reading memory.go: EnsureUser always writes Role: service.RoleUser for new rows and never touches Role for existing ones (Decision 11); usersByLogin is unexported so nothing outside package repository can seed a different role. Task 3's own access_repo_test.go (same package) reaches into MemoryRepository's unexported field via seedAdmin() specifically because handler-package tests cannot -- confirming both that the limitation is real and that MemoryRepository's admin-row behavior (EnsureUser preserving role/has_access across re-login) is already covered by Task 3's contract tests. Substituting in-package stubs for the access layer in access_test.go is safe and correctly scoped: it lets admin-gated routes be tested at all, while leaving the repository's own admin semantics to the layer that actually owns that coverage.
designDecisionNotes.3_AccessService_ListUsers: Additive method, does not touch or violate the UserRepository interface fixed by Task 2's Data Models (which already had ListUsers) or any AccessService method signature already in use. See minor finding above: no direct unit test plans to confirm it stays a thin passthrough as intended.
designDecisionNotes.4_UserRecord_json_tags: Confirmed against costing.go: all existing service-layer domain types use snake_case json tags (e.g. `calculator_mode`, `labor_minute_rate`). Adding snake_case tags to UserRecord matches house style exactly. No collision: grepped every UserRecord reference outside test files -- all are Go-native struct literals/field access in repository.go and service/access.go, none rely on encoding/json against UserRecord today, so adding tags is purely additive. Indirectly locked down by access_test.go's accessMeResponsePayload/adminUsersPayload structs, which decode the real JSON response and check exact field names.
designDecisionNotes.5_TDD_anchor_wording_discrepancy: Verified by reading Decision 18's text in tech-spec.md and the current normalizePath implementation in metrics.go: the rule collapses the segment immediately after '/admin/users/', not the whole '/admin/{login}/' shape -- so the correct target is '/api/v1/admin/users/:id/access', preserving the 'users' segment. tasks/5.md's TDD Anchor prose ('/api/v1/admin/:id/access', dropping 'users') is the one that's wrong, not the implementer's interpretation. metrics_test.go's TestNormalizePath_AdminUsersLoginCollapses correctly asserts '/api/v1/admin/users/:id/access' across five distinct login shapes (short, admin login from migration 004, numeric, Cyrillic-with-space) plus a cardinality-collision test and an existing-rules-unchanged regression suite. The implementer made the right call; tasks/5.md's wording should be corrected/noted in decisions.md, the test should not be changed to match the task's prose.
designDecisionNotes.6_fixed_slug_400_bodies: Consistent with Decision 17's spirit (no internal error text in any response) and does not contradict classifyDomainError/Task 4's existing domain-error handling -- decodeJSON errors are a distinct source that never flows through writeAPIDomainError today, so this is a new, narrower convention rather than a conflicting one, and is strictly more conservative than the pre-existing writeAPIError(w,400,err.Error()) pattern used for costing routes elsewhere in http.go (which Task 4's decisions.md already flagged as worth tightening later). See major finding above: this design choice currently has no test asserting the response body, only the status code.
